title.narrative: Project to Enhance Assistive Device Manufacturing Capacity for Injured Workers in Punjab, Pakistan

description.narrative:
This project aims to support the overcoming of disabilities and the social reintegration of injured workers by strengthening the capacity to manufacture rehabilitation assistive devices and providing customized rehabilitation services in Punjab, Pakistan. To achieve this, the project establishes a self-sustaining local manufacturing and integrated rehabilitation system, utilizing Mayo Hospitalthe only facility in Punjab with a rehabilitation assistive device manufacturing centeras its central hub.
The specific project is broadly composed of three main components:
1. Improvement of Infrastructure and Operational Environment for Manufacturing Rehabilitation Assistive Devices: The interior space of the manufacturing center at Mayo Hospital will be renovated to create an optimal clinical and production environment. Furthermore, modern machinery and core equipment will be supplied to enable the independent local production of low-cost, highly functional pneumatic rehabilitation devices. A systematic maintenance framework will also be established to ensure the long-term, stable operation of the newly introduced equipment.
2. Cultivation of Professionals in Manufacturing Rehabilitation Assistive Devices: A professional training curriculum tailored to local conditions will be developed, alongside the establishment of a mid-to-long-term human resource development roadmap. In particular, the project will focus on training prosthetist/orthotist 'Master Trainers' who will receive advanced technology transfers from Korea and lead local education initiatives. Centered around these Master Trainers, professional qualification courses will be regularized to lay the foundation for a sustainable, independent technical workforce.
3. Capacity Building for Integrated Clinical Rehabilitation Services for Injured Workers: Going beyond the simple provision of devices, a multidisciplinary approach encompassing physical therapy, occupational therapy, and psychological counseling will be applied. Expert consulting on the implementation of computerized systems and operational protocols will be provided to ensure the successful settlement of patient-customized integrated rehabilitation services in the region. Additionally, continuous technical cooperation between the two countries, including regular Korea-Pakistan workshops and academic exchanges, will be promoted with the overarching goal of advancing the rehabilitation system for injured workers in Pakistan.
